title: Aquatic Momentum Exchange Lab
description: A split-environment physics lab where a horse gallops along a riverside dock and a BarramundiFish swims in an adjacent water channel. The user configures mass, velocity, and angle parameters for both entities, then triggers elastic and inelastic collisions via a shared pendulum mechanism at the water's edge, observing conservation of momentum and kinetic energy across the land-water boundary with full undo/redo support.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader from CDN. Load BarramundiFish.glb and horse.glb. Scene setup: a flat dock platform on the left (brown plane) and a translucent blue water channel on the right, separated by a thin barrier wall. Place the horse on the dock and the fish in the water, both facing the barrier. Add a large pendulum sphere hanging above the barrier that transfers momentum between them. Camera: perspective at 45-degree angle, OrbitControls enabled. Lighting: ambient light plus two directional lights with shadows enabled on a soft blue-gray background. Physics UI: an HTML overlay panel with sliders for horse mass (50-500kg), fish mass (1-20kg), horse velocity (1-15 m/s), fish velocity (1-10 m/s), collision type toggle (elastic/inelastic), launch angle slider (-30 to 30 degrees), and a restitution coefficient slider (0-1). Add Launch, Reset, Undo, and Redo buttons. When Launch is pressed, animate the horse sliding toward the barrier, striking the pendulum, which swings and hits the fish, transferring momentum according to conservation laws. Display real-time momentum vectors as colored arrows (ArrowHelper) on both objects and show numeric readouts of momentum (p=mv) and kinetic energy (0.5mv²) for each entity. The user must: adjust horse mass, set horse velocity, set fish mass, set fish velocity, choose collision type, set angle, set restitution, launch, observe results, undo to previous state, change one parameter, and relaunch. Track all parameter states in a history stack supporting at least 5 undo/redo levels. After collision, both objects should move at physically correct post-collision velocities with smooth animation. Add a momentum conservation verification bar at the bottom showing total momentum before and after with a green checkmark when conserved within 1% tolerance.
